name: FT-897D
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not a Yaesu publication and not affiliated with Yaesu.
verified: Compiled from the Yaesu FT-897D Operating Manual, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. Only part of the numbered menu could be read; the rest is left out.
specs: 0.1 to 56 MHz, 76 to 108, 118 to 164, and 420 to 470 MHz
160 through 6 m including 60 m on US sets, plus 2 m and 70 cm
CW, AM, SSB, FM, and packet at 1200 and 9600 baud
100 W HF and 6 m, 50 W on 2 m, 20 W on 70 cm. AM carrier 25, 12.5 and 5 W
Drops automatically to 20 W, and 10 W on 70 cm
13.8 V DC plus or minus 15 per cent. The optional internal pack is 13.2 V, 4500 mAh
Two SO-239, one for HF and 6 m, one for 2 m and 70 cm
About 8.6 lb without the battery, antenna or microphone
None. A menu item chooses between an external tuner and an ATAS antenna
CAT and linear jack, 8-pin mini DIN, shared with the tuner and ATAS
keys: Hold one second to switch on or off. A tap engages fast tuning.
Tap changes the multi-function row. Hold one second enters the menu.
Act on the displayed row. There are seventeen rows, lettered a to q.
Detented. Tunes, picks memories, and scrolls the rows and menu items.
Tap jumps to the noise reduction row. Hold one second reaches the microphone equaliser.
LSB, USB, CW, CW reverse, AM, FM, digital, packet.
Switches VFO and memory. Hold to store the VFO contents.
Tap turns on the clarifier, plus or minus 9.99 kHz. Hold one second turns on IF shift.
RF gain or squelch, set by menu item 080.
quick: Memory write, scan skip, and channel naming.
Digital noise reduction, notch, and bandpass.
quick_right: tap F, then SELECT to scroll
tasks: Tap F to the memory row, tap MW for memory check, then hold MW one second to write the VFO into the selected register.
Tap V/M into memory mode, then SELECT to the channel.
Tap F to the scan row, tap SCN to start scanning upward. Tap again to stop.
Tap F to the VFO row, tap SPL.
Tap F to the repeater row. RPT sets the shift direction; hold RPT one second to reach menu 076 for the shift size. Hold the tone key one second to reach menu 083 for the tone frequency.
Hold the function key while switching the power on. Menu settings return to default and the memory channels survive. This is the one to reach for in the field.
Hold V/M while switching the power on. Memories go, along with a handful of menu items.
Hold HOME while switching the power on. A full processor reset of memories and settings.
trouble: Repeater shift size. Reached directly by holding the shift key.
Decides whether the concentric knob is squelch or RF gain.
CTCSS tone. Reached directly by holding the tone key.
notes: The same jack drives the tuner, the ATAS antenna and the computer, so they contend. Decide once what is plugged in and write it below.
A hundred watts from a portable battery is a short outing. Most of what this radio does well in the field it does at thirty or forty.
No internal tuner. Whatever you put up has to be resonant or matched by something you carried in.
The detachable head is a connector, and connectors fail. Carry the spare cable or accept that a bad day ends early.
Hold the function key while powering on and your menu settings go back to default but your memories survive. It is worth knowing which of the three resets is which before you need one.
